match.reason: None of the bank points teach the historical idea of early government action on the physical environment, such as clean water, sewerage and housing, as the origin of Australia's health improvements; they cover health promotion, global goals, health concepts, community resources and the Ottawa Charter.

draft.title: Old public health
card: Old public health was the first wave of government action on health, mainly in the 1800s and early 1900s. It tackled the physical environment that made people sick.

Governments improved clean water supplies, sewerage, rubbish removal and housing standards. In Australia, cities such as Melbourne and Sydney built sewers and piped water as infectious diseases spread in crowded towns.
These measures cut the spread of infectious diseases such as cholera and typhoid, which pass between people through dirty water and poor sanitation.
The focus was on the whole population's surroundings, not on treating one patient at a time. Old public health did not set out to change personal habits, such as diet or smoking.
draft.remember: Old public health improved health by fixing the physical environment, such as water, sewerage and housing.

a.q: Which action is an example of old public health?
opts: Building a sewerage system for a growing city
Running a television ad about healthy eating
Opening a hospital ward for heart surgery
Training people to read food labels
a.why: A sewerage system changes the physical environment and stops disease spreading through waste and dirty water. The hospital ward treats people who are already ill, so it does not fit old public health.
a.clue: Look for the option that changes the physical surroundings of a whole population.

b.q: In the 1880s a colonial government in Australia set rules for ventilation and overcrowding in city housing. Why is this old public health?
opts: It improved the physical environment to reduce disease
It treated people who had caught an infectious disease
It taught residents to change their own health habits
It gave residents control over decisions about their health
b.why: Rules on ventilation and crowding changed the physical conditions people lived in, which reduced the spread of disease. It is not about treating illness or changing habits, which were not the focus of old public health.
b.clue: Ask what the rules changed: the setting, or the person.

a.best: Building a sewerage system for a growing city

b.best: It improved the physical environment to reduce disease

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. Some VCE textbooks also count hygiene education as old public health, but the card only rules out changing habits such as diet or smoking, which is accurate.
